model: One YouTube channel I follow is Kurzgesagt, which is a German science channel with short animated videos in English. I came across it about five years ago, when a friend sent me a video about black holes, and I ended up binge-watching about ten videos that same night. Each video tends to focus on one big question, like how the immune system works or what would happen if the sun disappeared. What I like most is how they break down complex ideas into something anyone can follow, but they still go quite in-depth. It seems to me that they strike a balance between entertainment and education really well, because the animation is bright and funny, but the science is carefully researched. They actually list their sources for each video, which I'd say is quite rare on YouTube. These days I usually watch it on my commute, since the videos are only ten or fifteen minutes long, which is perfect for the bus ride to work. Arguably, the storytelling is what keeps me hooked, because every video feels like a small adventure. I've learned a lot from it, and to some extent it's broadened my horizons, especially about space and biology, which I didn't study at school. It's also helped my English, because they use quite advanced vocabulary but explain it clearly. So overall, it's one of the few channels I genuinely never skip.
